description: The rep assumes a single signer; the customer corrects mid-sentence to joint approval by two people.

turns.text: So Dana's the one who signs off on this, right?
Dana's... well, actually it's Dana and our COO, Raj Patel. Both of them have to sign before anything goes out.
Okay, so two signatures. Good to know.
Yeah. And honestly, uh, Dana usually follows Raj's lead, but formally it needs both.
Got it. I'll make sure the paperwork has both signature blocks.

evidence.quote: it's Dana and our COO, Raj Patel. Both of them have to sign before anything goes out.

decisionMaker.rationale: Joint sign-off is stated explicitly and reaffirmed. The rep's Dana-only assumption is SUPERSEDED by the mid-sentence correction. Collapsing to Raj only ('Dana usually follows Raj's lead') would be wrong.

notes: Illustrative schema-validation case drafted by Claude. NOT part of the benchmark.
